headline: Jalen Brunson converts tiebreaking 4-point play, scores 31 as Knicks win 15th straight over Raptors
text: TORONTO -- — Jalen Brunson converted a tiebreaking four-point play with 1:25 left in the fourth quarter, Karl-Anthony Towns had 16 points and 16 rebounds and the New York Knicks beat Toronto 111-102 on Tuesday night, their 15th consecutive win over the Raptors. Brunson scored 31 points. He shot 10 for 22, made 4 of 11 from 3-point range and went 7 for 7 at the free throw line. Mikal Bridges scored 17 points, OG Anunoby had 16 against his former team and Landry Shamet added 12 as the defending NBA champions swept the two-game series and won for the sixth time in eight games. Toronto’s Ja’Kobe Walter scored a season-high 25 points and made a career-best seven 3-pointers on 12 attempts, but was called for a flagrant foul on Brunson’s 3 late in the fourth. The Raptors last beat New York nearly four years ago, a 125-116 home win on Jan. 22, 2023. RJ Barrett scored 22 points for Toronto, Scottie Barnes had 20 and Immanuel Quickley added 14. The Raptors have lost five straight, letting double-digit leads slip away in each of the past four. Toronto dropped to 3-9 in 12 games without Kawhi Leonard , who remains sidelined because of a swollen left knee. In a pregame statement Tuesday, the Raptors said Leonard “has progressed in his strength and conditioning program” but provided no timetable for his return other than saying another update will come next week. Toronto led 48-35 after a driving basket by Barnes with 5:07 left in the second but the Knicks reclaimed the lead by scoring 19 consecutive points. Walter was 4 for 5 from distance in the third to help the Raptors take an 83-80 lead to the fourth. After going scoreless in the past two games, New York’s Josh Hart finished with five points. Up next Knicks: At Minnesota on Thursday. Raptors: Host Washington on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: McDaniels scores with 2.6 seconds left to lift Timberwolves to 106-105 win over Trail Blazers
text: MINNEAPOLIS -- — Jaden McDaniels hit a go-ahead layup with 2.6 seconds remaining after Minnesota stole a Portland inbounds pass and the Timberwolves rallied to beat the Trail Blazers 106-105 on Tuesday night. Portland led for nearly the entire fourth quarter before the Wolves mounted a furious comeback. Ayo Dosunmu hit a clutch 3-pointer with 50 seconds remaining to cut the lead to 105-104, setting up McDaniels' big shot. Portland's Damian Lillard had a look at a game-winning shot, but Minnesota's Trey Lyles blocked it with a second remaining. The teams also played Monday, with the Wolves winning 106-98 . Dosunmu led all scorers with a season-high 30 points to pace Minnesota's offense. McDaniels' winner gave him 22 points in the game, while LaMelo Ball chipped in 18 points and nine assists for the Wolves. Lillard found his shot Tuesday after going 2 for 15 in Monday's loss. The veteran guard hit 5 of 11 shots from deep and was 8 of 19 from the floor to lead the Blazers with 25 points. Jrue Holiday added 23 off the bench. Portland was without star Deni Avdija , who sat out Tuesday with a sore foot. He had 27 points and eight boards in Monday's loss to the Wolves. Minnesota was also down a starter Tuesday, as Jonathan Kuminga was ruled out with a right shoulder contusion. Kuminga took a knee to the shoulder in the fourth quarter of Monday's game. The Timberwolves, who entered Tuesday with the worst free throw percentage in the league (69%), missed 12 free throws. Minnesota big man Rudy Gobert , who had 18 points and 15 rebounds Monday against Portland, was a non-factor Tuesday. Foul trouble limited him to four minutes in the first half. He was held scoreless for the first time this season. Up next Trail Blazers: At Milwaukee on Thursday. Timberwolves: Host the New York Knicks on Thursday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Cunningham, Jenkins lead surge as Pistons snap Spurs' 12-game winning streak with 105-93 victory
text: SAN ANTONIO -- — Cade Cunningham scored 27 points, Daniss Jenkins had 21 of his 25 in the second half and the Detroit Pistons snapped San Antonio's 12-game winning streak, toppling the Spurs 105-93 on Tuesday night. Victor Wembanyama had 25 points and 18 rebounds for San Antonio, which had not lost since Oct. 23, when it fell to 0-2. Spurs guard Dylan Harper finished with 20 points but exited with 53 seconds remaining after his left foot slid out from under him and he tumbled to the court. His status is unknown. Ausur Thompson finished with 14 points, 12 assists, nine rebounds and five steals for Detroit, which overcame a sluggish start to win after getting swept by San Antonio last season. The Pistons outscored the Spurs 52-39 in the second and third quarters while shooting 51%. San Antonio lost for the first time when leading by double digits. Wembanyama had 10 points in the opening quarter, highlighted by throwing the ball off the backboard over an outstretched Thompson to assist on his own left-handed dunk. San Antonio had five dunks in the first quarter but it was Cunningham who provided the exclamation with a one-handed slam against a late-closing Wembanyama. Detroit went on a 21-7 run in the second quarter, closing with a 13-5 burst when Wembanyama sat, to tie the game at 47 after trailing by 14 in the period. The Spurs outscored the Pistons by 12 when Wembanyama was on the court in the first half and were minus-12 when he sat. Thompson and Cunningham combined for 21 points in the second quarter as Detroit outscored San Antonio 29-21 in taking its first lead at 55-54 into halftime. Detroit was without Jalen Duren (strained right hamstring), Duncan Robinson (strained left quadriceps) and Isaiah Joe (right hip contusion). Up next Pistons: At New Orleans on Wednesday. Spurs: Host Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Brice Sensabaugh scores 40 points and leads huge 4th quarter as Jazz beat Clippers for 2nd win
text: INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Brice Sensabaugh scored a season-high 40 points, including 25 in the fourth quarter, and the Utah Jazz beat the Los Angeles Clippers 132-107 on Tuesday night for just their second victory of the season. Sensabaugh sparked Utah's 44-point fourth quarter and Keyonte George added 30 points and 11 assists for the Jazz, who improved to 2-13 with their first win since beating New Orleans on Oct. 23 in their second game of the season. Utah had been 0-6 on the road. Sensabaugh came off the bench to finish three points shy of his career high. He shot 10 for 11 in the fourth quarter, 5 for 6 from 3-point range, and finished 16 for 21, including 8 for 11 behind the arc. He also grabbed 11 rebounds. The Jazz were an incredible 18 for 22 (81.8%) in the final 12 minutes. Brook Lopez scored 23 points for the Clippers, who had won two in a row. Darius Garland and Rui Hachimura both had 20. The Jazz led by 12 early in the second quarter, but their lead was just 88-86 going to the fourth. Rookie Keaton Wagler 's three-point play to start the period gave the Clippers the lead, but it was all Utah from there. Sensabaugh made consecutive 3-pointers to give the Jazz a 103-93 and they kept pouring it on, outscoring the Clippers 44-21. Mo Bamba had 15 points and 10 rebounds for the Jazz, while rookie Darryn Peterson had 13 points. Up next Jazz: Visit the Lakers on Wednesday. Clippers: Visit San Antonio on Thursday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Quentin Grimes scores 47, forces OT with 10th 3-pointer as Lakers rally past Hornets 118-114
text: LOS ANGELES -- — Quentin Grimes scored a career-high 47 points and forced overtime on his 10th 3-pointer with 1.7 seconds left in regulation before the Los Angeles Lakers finished off their ninth consecutive victory, 118-114 over the Charlotte Hornets on Tuesday night. Luka Doncic had 36 points and seven assists for the Lakers, who trailed by 18 in the second half before roaring back to remain unbeaten in November despite playing without injured Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler . Grimes scored 21 points in a phenomenal fourth quarter, leading the short-handed Lakers out of a lifeless performance. Los Angeles' new guard also made the most 3s of his career and joined Kobe Bryant as the only Lakers to make 10 3-pointers in a game. Brandon Miller scored 28 points and Naz Reid had 28 points and 11 rebounds for the Hornets. Charlotte kept Miller and Coby White , who scored 19 points, on the bench throughout overtime of their ninth loss in 10 games. The Lakers held Charlotte scoreless in the final 4:24 of overtime, but the Lakers also failed to score for three minutes. Grimes finally forced a turnover by Royce O'Neale on an inbounds play with 17.4 seconds left and made two free throws to ice it. The Lakers sat two of their top three scorers with injuries to begin a stretch of three home games in four days. Reaves missed his second straight game with a bruised heel, while Kessler missed his first game of the season with leg soreness. Grayson Allen sat out for Charlotte with concussion-like symptoms. He took a hit to the head during the Hornets’ loss to the Clippers on Sunday. After the Lakers tied it on Doncic’s fifth 3-pointer with 3:05 left in regulation, Charlotte went back ahead 110-106 with 20 seconds left — but Grimes made a layup and White missed one of two free throws before Doncic found Grimes for the tying 3. Up next Hornets: At Atlanta on Friday. Lakers: Host Utah on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
